long_biography.plain_text:
In 1971, as French sugar distribution consolidated, Gérard Bauche became chairman of the new Société industrielle et commerciale de sucrerie. The enterprise grouped six producers and was expected to market about a tenth of France's sugar output. He combined that role with the presidency of the national sugar-trade syndicate.

That chairmanship capped a career spanning production, brokerage, trading and beet cultivation. Bauche had served as director-general of the Villeron sugar works and chairman and chief executive of the Cambrai works. From 1965 he also headed the industry's statistical studies bureau. Moving between factories, merchants and sector bodies, he helped organise a trade adjusting to greater concentration and a common European market.
